explanation: Process a breadth-first queue one level at a time. Snapshot the queue size before each level so its newly enqueued children are placed in the following output group.
spaceComplexity: O(w) auxiliary queue space for maximum tree width w, plus O(n) output.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: At the beginning of a level, the queue contains that level’s nodes from left to right. Processing exactly its saved size emits precisely those nodes, while enqueuing each left child before its right child builds the next level in left-to-right order. Thus the invariant holds for the next iteration, and every node appears in exactly one output level.
walkthrough: For [16, 7, 25, 2, 11, null, 30], the queue first holds only 16, producing [16]. Its children produce [7, 25]. Their nonnull children, enqueued left to right, produce [2, 11, 30]. Return [[16], [7, 25], [2, 11, 30]].
edgeCases: Null input yields no levels, rather than one empty level.
Missing children are skipped without shifting a node into the wrong level.
The saved queue size keeps newly added children out of the current level.
